story.title: Three promises about one word
story.text: The word has three sources. The model's own stream says whether it is thinking or writing. A tool says researching, delegating or working, by what kind of tool it is. A retry and a compaction name themselves. Anything that says nothing new leaves the word as it was. These three lines are the first step of the spec, and they can be met before any screen exists.

story.title: Three tests that need nothing else
story.text: Each promise has its own test in test/cli-doing.test.mjs. All three do the same thing: hand a word and an event to one function and check the word that comes back. They import only that function, so they run without a runtime or a screen. The second test passes a whole `hobkin session` command, path and flags included, and expects delegating.

story.title: doingAfter: from an event to a word
story.text: This function is the whole rule. It takes the word so far and one event of the turn, and returns the word after it. It keeps no state of its own, so the same event always gives the same word. A streamed piece and a tool start go to two helpers. The end of a tool or of a compaction reads as thinking, a retry as retrying, a compaction as compacting. Any other event returns the word unchanged, which is the last sentence of A3.

story.title: Two helpers, one for each kind of event
story.text: streamedDoing reads the kind of a streamed piece: thinking reads as thinking, text as writing, and the start of a tool call as working. For any other piece it returns null, and doingAfter keeps the word it had. toolDoing reads a tool start. A tool that reads or searches is researching. A bash command that runs `hobkin session` is delegating, wherever hobkin is installed. Every other tool is working.

story.title: A rule that was already there
story.text: toolDoing does not decide what counts as research. It asks searchingTool in mood.mjs, which matches tool names such as read, grep, find, search and fetch. The face already uses that function to look like it is searching, and the snapshot already calls it. Using it here means the face and the row cannot disagree about the same tool. The function itself did not change.

story.title: The runtime keeps the word for one turn
story.text: connectMain is where the runtime listens to the main session. One new line passes every event to doingAfter and keeps the result as mainDoing, next to the tool name it already kept. The other change is in send. When the turn ends, however it ends, the finally block that already forgets the tool name sets mainDoing to null. A word left over from a finished turn would be false.

story.title: The promise that the word gets out
story.text: A4 asks for the word on the snapshot while the turn runs, and null after it. Its test opens an application through the suite's fixture. It tells the main session a piece of thinking and reads doing: thinking. It tells it that a read tool started and reads researching. Then it sends a message, waits for the turn to finish, and reads null.

story.title: One field on the snapshot
story.text: The screen reads the snapshot, a plain object the application builds again on every refresh. project is the method that builds it, and this change adds one line there: doing is the runtime's word, or null when there is none. It sits beside busy, searching and tooling, which the face already reads.

story.title: The row
story.text: workingRow builds the row from three things: the spinner frame, hobkin in the agent's color, and "is researching…" in dim text, with the word taken from snapshot.doing. Before the first event there is no word yet, so it falls back to thinking. On the right it shows how long the turn has run. elapsed formats that time and was already in the file: 15s under a minute, then minutes and seconds.

story.title: Where the row goes, and when
story.text: renderFooter builds the lines at the bottom of the screen: the input, the tips and the status. It builds the row only in Chat, with the input on screen, while hobkin is connected and busy. Then it puts the row first, above the input, whether or not the face is drawn beside it. The two removed lines are the two returns that now start with the row.

story.title: The test that draws the screen
story.text: A5 is the promise a person can see. Its test builds the dashboard from a busy snapshot whose word is researching, moves the clock 15 seconds, and draws an 80 by 24 screen. It looks for "hobkin is researching… 15s" and checks that the input starts on the next row. Then it updates the snapshot twice: with no word the row says thinking, and with busy off the row is gone.

story.title: One promise with no proof
story.text: A6 says the row gives way when a question or a card takes the input's place. The code does this: renderFooter returns for a card, a question or a choice before it builds the row. No test in this change checks it, so the line shows as unproven. The changelog states the same behavior, which makes a test for it worth adding.

story.title: Said in the guide and the changelog
story.text: Two files say it in words. The guide gains a paragraph on the row above the input, placed before the paragraph about the face. The changelog gains an entry under 2026-11-03, and it adds one thing the guide leaves out: the row also goes when a question takes the input's place. Neither file changes behavior.

closing: What this change leaves alone, and two questions it leaves open.
